pairs.subject: pipeline-dag
pairs.evidence: crates/server/src/triggers.rs:633 Trigger hook evaluation resolves unhandled predicate failures and malformed outputs to fail-open execution by default rather than halting the pipeline.

techniques.evidence: crates/server/src/triggers.rs:384 Predicate plugin hooks default to fail-open (fire) on error or malformed output rather than halting or routing to an error branch.
crates/server/src/triggers.rs:51 Acyclicity is not verified statically at authoring time; cycle detection is deferred to runtime by checking a provenance chain during hop execution.
crates/server/src/triggers.rs:1394 Unfired trigger branches do not produce skipped node executions in a graph run; non-matching conditions merely record a ledger row and continue.
crates/server/src/triggers.rs:934 Payload filters evaluate only local in-memory JSON data without remote calls or timeouts; compound condition trees with external leaves are not present.
crates/server/src/triggers.rs:517 Triggers support only synchronous plugin hook slots without pause-and-gate nodes or durable suspension awaiting human or external approval.
crates/server/src/triggers.rs:1543 Spend budget and attempt limits are passed to enqueue options, but node classes do not declare determinism or effect contracts.
crates/server/src/triggers.rs:940 Triggers handle inbound ingress events rather than outbound network adapter calls leaving the system boundary.
crates/server/src/triggers.rs:222 Triggers are individually authored reactive edges rather than graphs synthesized by an automated planner.

pairs.registryProposal: The pipeline-dag standard states that agent chaining through event subscriptions is a distinct subject where topology emerges from subscriptions rather than an authored graph document (lines 34-39). The standard should clarify whether event-driven reactive trigger chains (edge-list DAGs) are governed by pipeline-dag or belong to an event-routing/chaining standard.
